subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 42-year-old woman with a newly diagnosed soft tissue sarcoma undergoes tumor-cell culture studies. Investigators observe that DNA synthesis begins simultaneously at many sites along each chromosome and proceeds in both directions from each site, and that these sites share AT-rich consensus sequences.
question: Which of the following best describes origins of replication in human cells?

options.text: Each chromosome contains a single origin of replication
They are GC-rich sequences recognized by DNA ligase
They are located exclusively within telomeres
They are used only for synthesis of the lagging strand
They are multiple AT-rich consensus sequences that permit simultaneous bidirectional replication

explanation_correct: Eukaryotes have multiple origins of replication per chromosome, whereas prokaryotes typically have a single origin. Origins are AT-rich consensus sequences (AT-rich regions also occur in promoters), and replication proceeds bidirectionally from each origin.

explanation_incorrect.A: A single origin per chromosome is characteristic of prokaryotes, not human cells.
explanation_incorrect.B: Origins are AT-rich, not GC-rich, and DNA ligase does not recognize origins.
explanation_incorrect.C: Origins are distributed along the chromosome and are not confined to telomeres.
explanation_incorrect.D: Each origin fires to support synthesis of both strands; leading and lagging strands are made at each replication fork.

educationalObjective: Human chromosomes contain multiple AT-rich origins of replication that allow simultaneous bidirectional DNA synthesis.
